newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary denies it plans change devaluation system.
newsitem.headline: Hungary denies it plans change devaluation system.

text.p: Hungary's Finance Ministry on Friday denied statements from the largest opposition party that there are official plans to change the current system of pre-announced crawling peg devaluation.
"The monthly devaluations will continue in the first half of 1997 according to the current system, and the monthly rate will not be larger than 1.2 percent," the Finance Ministry said in a statement.
The Ministry reacted to a Friday statement by Bela Szabadi, chairman of the economic expert team of the Independent Smallholders' Party (FKGP), who said the government planned a one-off devaluation.
Szabadi told a news conference that the devaluation would compensate the state budget for the loss of abolishing Hungary's seven percent import duty surcharge by June 1997.

The Finance Ministry said the aim of the government with introducing an eight percent surcharge last March was not to generate revenues for the state budget, but to rein in the then soaring current account and trade deficits.
"The current monthly 1.2 percent devaluation is appropriate to encourage exports properly and not to cause an increase of import competition which could be unmanageable," the Finance Ministry said.
